Issued at 251 PM CDT Sun Aug 23 2026

Currently...

An upper level shortwave disturbance sliding southeast across 
portions of the Central Plains has resulted in a damp end to the 
weekend for a good chunk of the forecast area today...with activity 
taking its sweet time pushing through eastern portions this 
afternoon. This disturbance is embedded in continued larger scale 
northwesterly flow...set up in a well amplified pattern across the 
CONUS. The main area of high pressure continues to sit over the 
Desert SW, with ridging extending northward through the 
Rockies...sandwiched between a large area of low pressure spinning 
over the Great Lakes with troughing dominating the East Coast, and 
another area of low pressure pushing east along the WA/Canada 
border. Outside of at times heavy rainfall rates, this activity 
hasn't amounted to a whole lot...as better instability has remained 
focused off to the west of the forecast area. Satellite imagery has 
shown the development of quite a range of cloud cover across the 
area...with mostly cloudy skies across the eastern half, more sun 
further west. This has resulted in mid-afternoon temps ranging from 
the mid 60s in the east to the low 80s in the far southwest...though 
those eastern areas still have the potential for late day highs if 
the cloud cover diminishes. At the surface, the forecast area sits 
between high pressure gradually working its way east and a deeper 
trough axis along the High Plains...bringing southeasterly winds 
this afternoon, at times gusting near 20 MPH. 

Tonight into Monday...

For most locations, the forecast for this evening and tonight 
remains dry. Models continue to show the potential for at least 
scattered showers/storms developing late tonight (mainly 
around/after midnight) into the early morning hours on 
Monday...focused along the edge of a SSWrly low-level jet. Models 
remain consistent showing the best potential for this activity is 
across eastern portions of mainly our Nebraska counties...but vary 
some on just how far west coverage actually gets. Chances remain in 
the 20-40 percent range, with overall lift looking to be on the 
weaker side, currently not expecting notable coverage of activity. 
Not out of the question that a few storm could be on the strong side 
with MUCAPE potentially around 1500 j/kg, but the threat for severe 
weather continues to look low. 

Any activity that lingers into the daytime hours on Monday is 
expected to diminish by mid-morning...with the remainder of the day 
and at least part of the evening currently dry. Models showing 
little change in the overall upper level pattern, with the main 
high/ridging remaining over the Desert SW and Rockies. Forecast has 
lighter winds turning more easterly through the day, speeds topping 
out around 10-15 MPH. Expecting to have a bump up in afternoon 
highs, with generally mid 80s across central/eastern portions of our 
NE counties, with upper 80s-low 90s further south and west.

Monday night into Tuesday...

A little more uncertainty with preciptiation chances works its way 
back into the forecast late Monday evening into the overnight hours. 
Looking aloft, models showing that upper level low currently over 
WA/Canad having continued trekking ENE...ending up over south-
central Canada by Monday evening. A southward extending sfc front 
(although on the weaker side) and shortwave energy looks to spark 
off afternoon thunderstorm development over portions of the Dakotas 
into the Sandhills...the main question then turning to how much of 
that activity works its way into our forecast area overnight. There 
are some notable differences between models...some showing little 
diminishment in activity as it moves in...others with notable waning 
with time. Made no changes to the NBM PoPs Monday night-Tuesday AM, 
which have a notable range from the 20 percent range in the ESE to 
50-60 percent range further WNW. At this point, this activity is not 
expected to be severe.

Some questions then linger through the daytime hours on Tuesday into 
evening/overnight...if activity does move in, how long into the day 
does it linger, and what impact could it have on the next expected 
round of thunderstorms to move through the region. Plenty of details 
to iron out in the next 48hrs...but additional shortwave energy is 
expected to fire off another round of thunderstorms off to our NW, 
but exactly where is a little uncertain at least partly due to where 
any sfc frontal boundaries may ultimately be/set up. There will be 
the potential for another MCS to sink SSE across the region...with 
models showing both better instability and shear developing to tap 
into. This will bring better potential for storms to be strong to 
severe...and the entire forecast area remains included in the SPC 
Day 3 Marginal/Slight risk areas, with the Slight risk area roughly 
from the Tri-Cities southwest-ward into western KS. 

Wednesday and on...
